why: The inserted binding (keep a noun head with any immediately following essential post‑nominal modifier) caused the model to avoid cuts that would split a head+modifier, so it often moved cuts earlier (placing the cut before the noun) to keep the noun+modifier together. That change helps very short pieces and list/title splits (bins ≤3/≤5, best examples) but harms longer, multi‑clause sentences (overall ≤99 negative and a big drop in rank for k=1) by fragmenting adjacent clauses and moving cuts into preceding material.
lesson: When adding a noun‑head+modifier binding, ensure it does not force earlier cuts that fragment adjacent clauses or long spans — only apply it when it can be satisfied without shifting cuts into preceding material.
